name: Opportunity rover
tagline: Built for a 90-day mission, Opportunity kept exploring Mars for nearly fifteen years before a planet-wide storm silenced it.
imageAlt: Illustrated archive portrait of Opportunity rover
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Search Meridiani Planum for evidence of past water and investigate the geology of Mars.
beats.achieved: Opportunity operated for almost 15 years, travelled more than 45 kilometres, and found strong evidence that liquid water once altered Martian rocks.
beats.ending: A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 blocked sunlight from reaching the rover's solar panels. After its last communication on June 10, NASA made repeated attempts to contact it. The mission was declared complete on February 13, 2019.
beats.now: Opportunity remains at Perseverance Valley on Mars, where its long journey ended.
beats.learned: The rover showed that small robotic explorers can far exceed their planned lifetimes and transformed our understanding of ancient water on Mars.
